name: Saint Augustine of Canterbury
history: A Roman monk sent by Pope Gregory the Great to bring the Gospel to the English. He landed in Kent in 597, was welcomed by King Æthelberht, whose Frankish queen Bertha was already a Christian, and baptised the king and many of his people. As first Archbishop of Canterbury he founded the Church from which English Christianity grew.
life: Augustine was prior of Gregory’s own monastery of Saint Andrew on the Caelian Hill when the pope chose him to lead some forty monks to England in 596. In Gaul they lost heart at the tales of a fierce people, and Augustine went back to ask that they be excused; Gregory sent him on with letters of encouragement. They landed on Thanet in 597. Bede tells us the king met them in the open air for fear of magic, listened, and allowed them to preach in Canterbury, where they prayed in the old church of Saint Martin. Æthelberht was baptised, and great numbers followed at Christmas. Augustine was consecrated bishop in Gaul, founded Christ Church and the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul at Canterbury, and set up sees at London and Rochester. Gregory advised him to purify pagan temples rather than destroy them. His talks with the bishops of the older British Church did not reach agreement. He died around 604.
prayerTo: Saint Augustine of Canterbury, you came to a strange land with fear and obeyed, and God made you the father of the faith in England. Pray for England and for her conversion, for bishops and missionaries, and for me, that I may obey when I am afraid and trust God to finish His work. Amen.
penance: Pray today for the conversion of England and for unity among Christians in this land. If you live near a church founded in Augustine’s time, visit it.
meditation: He turned back once, and was sent on again. Where have you turned back from what God asked, and are you ready to go on?
